newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-STARKS GIVES KNICKS VICTORY WITH LONG-RANGE BUZZER BEATER.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-STARKS GIVES KNICKS VICTORY WITH LONG-RANGE BUZZER BEATER.

text.p: John Starks drained a three-pointer at the buzzer to cap a frantic finish as the New York Knicks edged the Phoenix Suns a 95-94 on Tuesday.
A jumper by Jason Kidd had given Phoenix a 94-92 lead with 28 seconds to go and the Knicks wound down the clock inside 10 seconds.
Allan Houston missed a three-pointer, but the long rebound bounced to Starks, who dribbled behind the arc, gave a fake and let the winning shot go just before the buzzer.

"I pump faked, I took my time and squared up and knocked it down," said Starks, who scored 11 of his 15 points in the fourth quarter. "It felt real good. I was worried about the shot clock, not the shot."
"Danny Manning was right on him. He made a great pump fake to get open," said Knicks guard Chris Childs of the finish that had all the intensity of a playoff game.
Patrick Ewing had 31 points and 13 rebounds for the Knicks, who erased a 16-point third-quarter deficit to win for the 20th time in their last 21 home games.
"Everybody was jumping on (Starks)," Ewing said. "I thought we won the championship."
Wesley Person scored 22 points and Cedric Ceballos added 19 for the Suns, who led 70-54 with 6:30 left in the third quarter before the Knicks erupted with an 18-2 run.
In Chicago, Scottie Pippen pulled a Michael Jordan.
Pippen poured in a career-high 47 points on 19-of-27 shooting as the Bulls won their 17th straight home game, a 134-123 victory over the Denver Nuggets.
"I never really knew I was near my career high until the fans starting booing Phil (Jackson) for taking me out," said Pippen, who scored 18 points in the third quarter alone.
Jordan scored 24 points, Steve Kerr chipped in 18 and Dennis Rodman pulled down 13 rebounds for the Bulls.
Dale Ellis had 27 points and Antonio McDyess added 25 for Denver, which scored 44 points in the 77-point fourth quarter as the teams combined for the highest-scoring NBA contest this season.
In Philadelphia, Tim Hardaway scored 29 points and newly acquired Jamal Mashburn added 15 as the Miami Heat routed the 76ers 111-83 for their franchise-record 10th straight victory.
Alonzo Mourning recorded 14 points, 10 rebounds and six blocks for the Heat, who improved to 23-6 on the road.
Jerry Stackhouse scored 18 points and Don MacLean added 17 to pace the 76ers, who have dropped five in a row and 31 of their last 36 games.
At Utah, Karl Malone had 37 points, eight assists and seven rebounds as the Jazz pounded the plummeting San Antonio Spurs 113-105.
Malone nailed 12-of-17 shots from the field and John Stockton added 19 points and 10 assists as Utah shot 57 percent (43-for-76) en route to its 14th win in 16 games to improve to 24-2 at home.
Dominique Wilkins had 32 points and 12 rebounds and Vinny Del Negro added 28 points for the Spurs, who have lost four in a row and 10 of their last 11 games.
In Los Angeles, Malik Sealy scored 23 points to lead the Clippers to a 87-69 win over the undermanned Dallas Mavericks.
Rodney Rogers scored 11 points and Loy Vaught added 10 for the Clippers, who won for the fifth time in seven games.
Michael Finley scored 18 points and Derek Harper added 17 for the Mavericks, who did not yet have the services of the four players they acquired in a nine-player trade with New Jersey on Monday.
In Sacramento, Mahmoud Abdul-Rauf scored eight of his 16 points in the final 3:38 as the Kings beat the Minnesota Timberwolves 95-84.
Mitch Richmond scored 20 points and Olden Polynice added 17 and 21 rebounds to lead the Kings.

Tom Gugliotta had 28 points and 18 rebounds and Stephon Marbury added 21 points for Minnesota, which lost out on a chance to reach the .500 mark for the first time in team history later than the first month of the season.
